knowledge:
- key_parameters: formule=A symbolic description of the terms in the model (e.g., "Smoothing+QuartetEffect+FL+I(FL^2)+I(FL^3)+GC+I(GC^2)+I(GC^3)"). Allows users to exclude specific effects like PCR fragment length ;; confidence=The prediction interval used to flag and exclude poorly predicted quartets (default is 0.95) ;; iteration=The number of ITALICS iterations (default is 2) ;; param=The penalty term used in the GLAD kernel function (default is c(d=2)). Decreasing this parameter increases the number of identified breakpoints, which is recommended for low signal-to-noise ratio arrays ;; qlambda=The relative importance of geographical and statistical proximity in the GLAD segmentation process. Higher values allow detection of smaller alterations ;; bandwidth=The number of iterations performed in the GLAD algorithm. Smaller values run faster but lower the quality of the segmentation process
- alternatives: CNAT (Affymetrix Copy Number Analysis Tool), CNAG, and GIM. ITALICS is preferred over these methods because it iteratively and alternatively estimates biological and non-relevant effects, preventing the biological signal from biasing the estimation of systematic noise
- when_to_use: Appropriate for DNA copy number alteration and polymorphism studies using Affymetrix GeneChip Human Mapping 100K (XbaI and HindIII) or 500K (Sty and Nsp) sets, especially in cancer datasets where biological and non-relevant variations have similar amplitudes
- pitfalls: Setting the GLAD 'param' parameter to values smaller than 1 or 2 on chips with low signal-to-noise ratios can drastically increase the number of false positive alterations detected. Spatial artifacts and poorly predicted quartets must be properly flagged and excluded to avoid biasing the final copy number estimation

workflows.name: italics_normalization_and_calling
workflows.intent: Normalize Affymetrix GeneChip Human Mapping chips and call DNA copy number alterations using the iterative ITALICS algorithm.
workflows.stages: 1. Read the CEL file header to identify the chip type and platform ;; 2. Load the corresponding quartet effect reference data ;; 3. Retrieve SNP and quartet metadata for the platform ;; 4. Read CEL intensities and calculate quartet log ratios ;; 5. Add quartet effect information and map quartet-level data to SNP-level data ;; 6. Run the iterative ITALICS normalization and copy number calling ;; 7. Plot the normalized genomic profile
workflows.code:
ITALICSDataPATH <- attr(as.environment(match("package:ITALICSData",search())),"path")
filename <- paste(ITALICSDataPATH,"/extdata/HF0844_Xba.CEL", sep="")
headdetails <- readCelHeader(filename[1])
pkgname <- cleanPlatformName(headdetails[["chiptype"]])
quartetEffectFile <- paste(ITALICSDataPATH,"/extdata/Xba.QuartetEffect.csv", sep="")
quartetEffect <- read.table(quartetEffectFile, sep=";", header=TRUE)

snpInfo <- getSnpInfo(pkgname)
quartet <- getQuartet(pkgname, snpInfo)
tmpExprs <- readCelIntensities(filename, indices=quartet$fid)
quartet$quartetInfo$quartetLogRatio <- readQuartetCopyNb(tmpExprs)
quartet$quartetInfo <- addInfo(quartet, quartetEffect)
snpInfo <- fromQuartetToSnp(cIntensity="quartetLogRatio",
          quartetInfo=quartet$quartetInfo, snpInfo=snpInfo)

profilSNPXba <- ITALICS(quartet$quartetInfo, snpInfo,
     formule="Smoothing+QuartetEffect+FL+I(FL^2)+I(FL^3)+GC+I(GC^2)+I(GC^3)")

data(cytoband)
plotProfile(profilSNPXba, Smoothing="Smoothing", cytoband=cytoband)
